rules: R1 Master -14 LUFS +/-0.5, true peak <= -1.5 dBTP, never below -15 LUFS (YouTube turns loud files down but never turns quiet ones up; Ian Shepherd). Test: ebur128 peak=true. ep01 PASS (-14.0 LUFS, -1.5 dBTP).

R2 Music >= 15 LU under the voice in 90% of speech windows (median 18-22 LU); ambience >= 15 LU under it (Torcoli et al. 2019 JAES: >=10 LU commentary over music, >=15 LU over ambience; ordinary viewers want 4 LU more than engineers). Test: 3 s short-term loudness of each stem. ep01 PASS (median 18.9 LU, p10 15.6).

R3 Voice beats music+SFX by >= 15 dB at 1-4 kHz in >= 95% of speech windows; no SFX onset on a name, number or payoff word (Lang LC4MP: auditory memory suffers first under dense production). ep01 FAIL: 91.4% of windows, p5 12.4 dB; 83% of SFX started under speech; bell dings at 843.4 s and 845.9 s around the central question.

R4 No pumping: duck hold about 0.8-1.0 s plus a 0.5-0.8 s release, so music only rises in planned gaps of 1.2 s or more; <= 2 pump events/min (a release that is too fast 'snaps back up during natural pauses inside a sentence'). ep01 FAIL: 314 events, 18.6/min (mix.py has no hold).

R5 Hits that carry a beat must be audible on a phone: add a 250-700 Hz harmonic layer (energy above 250 Hz no more than 10 dB under the total) and place it in a voice gap; sub-only booms are decoration (phone speakers struggle below 200 Hz). ep01 FAIL: impact_deep keeps only -31.7 dB of its energy above 250 Hz and was used 8 times on reveals. In ep02, impact_deep is planned 7 times on hero-number words.

R6 Plan an energy map: tag each cue section low/mid/high; cue sections differ by >= 6 LU; final LRA 3-6 LU with the voice steady (Elwyn: 'all the same all the time... loses its impact'; Krotos: power comes from more dynamic range). ep01 FAIL: cue medians within 4.1 LU, LRA 2.3 LU, short-term spread 1.7 LU.

R7 'Thinking' music (pulse, no lead melody) goes under explanation; 'feeling' music only where earned, mostly in gaps and hero shots; alternate the two with no fixed ratio (Johnny Harris, How I Use Music; documentary composers prefer 'a subtle mood'). ep01 PARTIAL: lead melody was banned, but a reflective feeling cue (m09) ran under the densest explanation (782-875 s).

R8 Change the music audibly every 45-90 s, max 120 s unchanged; change at story turns, entering 0.5-2 s before the turn line, not on the word (NPR Throughline's Ramtin Arablouei: 'slightly before, where it's not so predictable'). ep01 FAIL: m03 185 s, m10 139 s, all 9 changes were identical crossfades. ep02 script: Ch3 (133 s) and Ch4 (122 s) need a section change.

R9 End cues on purpose (cadence, ring-out, or hard-out into a stop-down or hit); <= 1/3 plain crossfades (composer Miriam Cutler: 'whenever you get out, it's going to be noticed'). ep01 FAIL: 9 of 9 identical 2.5 s/3 s crossfades.

R10 Generate cues from ElevenLabs composition plans (chunks with duration_ms 3-120 s) whose boundaries sit on turns, drops and reveals; accept only if each planned event is within 0.5 s, otherwise edit at a bar line. ep01 FAIL: m01 asked for a drop at about 31 s; it came at 44.3-46.7 s. music.py does not support composition plans yet.

R11 Justify every cue and SFX with a stated job; run a remove-50% A/B (Arablouei: 'ask yourself why... If you don't, then don't do it', 'restraint is as important as laying it on'; Bill Weber: some scenes 'don't even need music'). ep01 FAIL: 340 SFX (20.2/min) with no recorded job.

R12 Stop-down before every hero reveal: the music bus drops >= 20 dB for 0.4-1.2 s (ramps <= 50 ms) ending on the reveal word, with ambience or a sub drone kept above the -45 dB silence gate; then the hit or new section lands on the word; about one per 60-90 s (Rareform stopdowns; Krotos 'lack of sound can be as gripping as an explosion'; Tony Volante). ep01 FAIL: no stop-down at any of the 4 key reveals; its only 2 dips were before gags.

R13 Every riser peaks within 1 frame of a hit, stop-down or reveal word and never runs on under narration; no two identical risers within 60 s (drains keep their riser per the playbook but use different rising devices). ep01 FAIL: only 1 of 8 risers resolved. ep02 script: drain risers 12 s apart (s005/s009) and 3.3 s apart (s048/s049).

R14 Build tension with more than one-shots: an 8 s+ build rising >= 4 LU into each chapter climax, using a pulse or ticking ostinato, a Shepard-style rising pitch, a sub drone and layered, blended place sound (Vox on Dunkirk; Throughline's 8-9 layer soundscape). ep01 PARTIAL: its tension came almost only from 8 riser one-shots.

R15 Make contrast survive YouTube Stable volume (on by default; 'balances the range between quiet and loud'): make drops by removing layers and changing register, not by level alone; check every reveal after a dynaudnorm pass. ep01 not checked.

R16 Sound the devices, not the text: SFX only on the playbook's devices (flights, counters and gauge, reveals, drains, standees) and gags; labels, pins and text enter silently; <= 3 SFX per 10 s of narration, about 10/min outside montages. ep01 FAIL: 20.2/min, 78 pop_ui on labels, 27 SFX in minute 1. ep02 script plans 8.2/min, which passes.

R17 Spot SFX to the final picture from the render's event log, within 1 frame; whoosh only where something moves (Kurzgesagt adds music and SFX last, after voice-over and animation). ep01 FAIL: SFX entries had no event ids; 83 identical soft whooshes.

R18 No identical repeats: >= 4 variants per SFX family, round-robin with seeded +/-1.5 semitones and +/-2 dB; no file more than twice in 60 s (Potter et al. 2018: the orienting response to a repeated production effect fades by its third onset). ep01 FAIL: 138 same-file repeats within 10 s (whoosh_soft x83, pop_ui x78).

R19 Give each place its own ambience bed (surf, wind, forest, deep-water pressure), continuous through cuts within the place, >= 15 LU under the voice, present under >= 50% of the runtime (Arablouei on sense of place; Gibney/Volante 'feel subconsciously'). ep01 FAIL: 61 s of ambience = 6% of runtime.

R20 Sound leads picture: the next place's ambience or cue starts 0.3-1.0 s before the cut at every change of place (Arablouei: bring sound in 'before you hear any kind of mention'). ep01 FAIL: no pre-laps; mix.json has no field for them.

R21 Gag sounds must be in-world and never cheap: the sound the on-screen object would make, in the gap after the line, <= 0.8 s, one per gag; ban meme stingers (record scratch, crickets, cartoon fall whistle, vine boom, sad trombone, a bell ding as the punchline). ep01 FAIL: cartoon fall in the hook at 17.5 s, 2 record scratches, crickets, 9 bell dings.

R22 Protected zones (1975 Halape deaths, Nihoa graves, Battle of Midway and its war graves). Across the whole scene, until the music changes: no stings, risers, musical hits, UI ticks, comic SFX or playful cue; realistic event sound is allowed. Hush from 1 s before each death or grave line to 10 s after it: ambience and one pad only. ep01 FAIL: a record scratch at 589.55 s inside the grief cue, 39 s after a death line. ep02 script: remove tick_soft on 'three miles down' (s138), 0.4 s before 'These are war graves'; add a music section change at s105 before the seal gag, 32 s after the Nihoa graves; drip_comic, line_tug and the thunk inside the Midway battle scene are the owner's call (swap for in-world sounds).

R23 Gate with numbers, then the owner's ears: audio_scan plus pump/min, SFX per minute and per 10 s, repeats, riser resolution, stop-downs at reveals, protected-zone SFX, 1-4 kHz margin and a phone check; then give the owner about 10 timestamps to listen to. No agent claims an ear verdict (playbook section 16). ep01 FAIL: none of these metrics existed.

It picks the best take per variant, trims leading silence to a 10 ms pre-roll, de-clicks beds, cuts end clicks, normalises to -20 LUFS with the peak at -2 dBFS or lower (the ep01 convention, 48 kHz 24-bit WAV) and records the measured sync point.
